run.question:
The checkout-service in production-eu-west-2 is throwing 500s. Please look at
app-264-prod-logs and find the root cause.

report.summary: No data for production-eu-west-2 was found: the only log index available, app-264-prod-logs, contains exactly three documents in the authorized window 2026-11-20T06:13:57Z–2026-11-21T06:13:57Z and every one of them carries cluster=staging-eu-west-2, environment=staging, region=eu-west-2, i.e. a different cluster from the one the question names. Because of that, nothing in this index can be named as the root cause of a production-eu-west-2 incident. WHAT WAS FOUND FOR THE DIFFERENT (STAGING) ENTITY: two ERROR lines from service checkout-service (2026-11-21T04:13:48Z 'Smoke test failed: deploy-v2.3.4 rollback in progress'; 2026-11-21T05:13:48Z 'POST /api/checkout returned 500: integration-test fixture stripe-test-key expired') plus one WARN from payment-service (2026-11-21T05:43:48Z 'Using mock provider for staging (stripe-mock)'), all labeled staging-eu-west-2. The staging-eu-west-2 Kubernetes cluster I can read does not corroborate them: its otel-demo/checkout deployment is revision 1 (created 2026-11-20T16:32:06Z, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout), no rollout or rollback occurred inside the window, the pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n is Running/Ready and its log lines for 05:13:57Z–06:13:57Z show successful PlaceOrder → payment → confirmation-email sequences, the payment pod shows completed transactions, all flagd fault-injection flags are at defaultVariant 'off', and the only events in the window concern app-101 loki/payment-api-101 and an Endpoints warning for a loki service in app-282. Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE) on every attempt, so error-rate, latency, alert and span-error evidence could not be checked for any cluster; that (together with the absent production-eu-west-2 data) is why this assessment is inconclusive rather than supported.

claims.text: The Elasticsearch source contains only one index, app-264-prod-logs (open, shipped by source 'otel-demo'); pattern '*' matched exactly one index.
app-264-prod-logs maps cluster, environment, region, service, level as keyword, message as text and timestamp as the date field (@timestamp is not mapped).

An aggregation over the whole authorized window for app-264-prod-logs matched 3 documents and returned exactly one cluster bucket, staging-eu-west-2 (3 docs), one environment bucket, staging (3 docs), and service buckets checkout-service (2) and payment-service (1); no production-eu-west-2 and no other cluster appears.

All three documents were returned in full, sorted ascending, each with cluster=staging-eu-west-2, environment=staging, region=eu-west-2: checkout-service ERROR 'Smoke test failed: deploy-v2.3.4 rollback in progress' at 2026-11-21T04:13:48Z, checkout-service ERROR 'POST /api/checkout returned 500: integration-test fixture stripe-test-key expired' at 2026-11-21T05:13:48Z, and payment-service WARN 'Using mock provider for staging (stripe-mock)' at 2026-11-21T05:43:48Z.

The 05:13:48Z checkout ERROR line's own text attributes that 500 to an expired integration-test fixture, 'stripe-test-key expired'; the line carries cluster=staging-eu-west-2, so this describes a staging fixture, not a production-eu-west-2 failure.

In the staging-eu-west-2 cluster, deployment otel-demo/checkout is ready 1/1, generation 1, deployment.kubernetes.io/revision '1', created 2026-11-20T16:32:06Z, with image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout; there is a single ReplicaSet checkout-6578865d87 (created 2026-11-20T16:32:06Z), so no deploy-v2.3.4 rollout or rollback happened there inside the window.

Staging-eu-west-2 pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n (owner ReplicaSet checkout-6578865d87) is Running with container ready=true, restartCount 1, started 2026-11-21T04:23:48Z; its last termination reason is recorded as Unknown with exit code 255 and no previous-container log lines were read.

Staging-eu-west-2 checkout application logs for 2026-11-21T05:53:19Z–06:13:42Z show repeated successful orders ('[PlaceOrder] ...', 'payment went through (transaction_id: ...)', 'order confirmation email sent to ...'); a regex filter 'error|500|fail|panic' over 05:13:57Z–06:13:57Z matched only 2 informational lines ('bill@example.com' confirmation and a transaction id containing '500'), i.e. no checkout 500 was logged by this pod in that hour.

Staging-eu-west-2 payment pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d logged 'Charge request received.' followed by 'Transaction complete.' for each sampled charge between 2026-11-21T05:16:04Z and 06:01:40Z; the error-filtered lines contain no error-level entry.

Every fault-injection flag in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (flagd flags productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad) has state ENABLED but defaultVariant 'off' in the staging-eu-west-2 cluster, so no injected checkout or payment fault was in effect there.

Kubernetes events in the readable cluster for the window (18 events, 05:28:04Z–06:06:19Z) involve only app-101 (Deployment loki ScalingReplicaSet, ReplicaSet loki SuccessfulCreate, Pod loki-66445c6d6f-drtbg Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started, Deployment payment-api-101 ScalingReplicaSet, Pod payment-api-101-8486559b69-v4v9b Created/Started/Killing) plus one Warning Endpoints FailedToCreateEndpoint for service app-282/loki; no event names any checkout object.

Against the hypothesis that the staging checkout errors reflect an active fault in the cluster I can read: that cluster's checkout pod logged only successful orders during the window, its deployment shows revision 1 with no rollout, and all flagd fault flags are 'off'.

Rejected as the production-eu-west-2 root cause: the expired 'stripe-test-key' fixture named in the 05:13:48Z checkout 500 line. The line's own labels place it in cluster staging-eu-west-2 / environment staging, so it cannot explain a 500 in the cluster the question names, and in the staging cluster I can read the matching payment path completed transactions normally.

Rejected as the production-eu-west-2 root cause: the 'deploy-v2.3.4 rollback in progress' smoke-test line. It is labeled staging-eu-west-2, and the staging cluster's checkout deployment has revision 1 only (single ReplicaSet, created 2026-11-20T16:32:06Z, image tag 2.0.2-checkout) with no rollout, so no v2.3.4 rollback is observable there and none can be attributed to production.

The checkout-service 500s reported for production-eu-west-2 remain unexplained: no log document, metric series or trace labeled production-eu-west-2 was retrievable in this run, so the fault could lie in a service or configuration that only the production cluster exposes (for example a payment-provider credential or a production-only fault-injection setting) — this is unverified.

Point the log shipper or index pattern for production-eu-west-2 at a reachable index (or confirm which index actually holds that cluster's documents, checking the document-level cluster/environment fields), then re-run the checkout error and trace analysis against it.

Restore the Prometheus and Jaeger paths (every query to target m0-otel-20260909 returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), then check checkout error-rate series such as traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name=...,status_code=...} and rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count per rpc_grpc_status_code to establish whether the production 500s originate in checkout's own handlers or in a dependency call.

gaps: No production-eu-west-2 data exists in the sources I could reach: the only index (app-264-prod-logs) holds just 3 documents in the window and all carry cluster=staging-eu-west-2 and environment=staging, so the named cluster's checkout-service 500s are unobserved.

Prometheus was unreachable for the whole run (get_all_labels, get_metric_names, get_label_values, list_prometheus_rules, get_prometheus_target, execute_prometheus_instant_query and metrics_range_query all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE with source_contact 'possible'), so error rates, latency, kube-state-metrics and alert state are unknown for every cluster.

Jaeger was unreachable for the whole run (traces_list_services, traces_search on checkout and on frontend all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so span-level errors and dependency edges for the failing requests are unknown.

Kubernetes access covers only cluster staging-eu-west-2; production-eu-west-2 objects (deployments, pods, events, configmaps) could not be read, so the production pod status, exit codes, events and application logs are unknown.

Change history is not integrated, so I cannot tell when the app-264-prod-logs documents were written relative to any production change, nor whether a production deployment or config change preceded the 500s.

The alert that started this investigation is not retrievable (list_prometheus_rules unavailable), so the onset time of the deviation in production-eu-west-2 is unknown; the 04:13:48Z and 05:13:48Z staging-eu-west-2 error lines cannot be used as the alert onset.

The staging-eu-west-2 checkout pod's earlier container instance left no readable log lines (previous stream bytes_read 0), so the cause of its single restart (last termination reason Unknown, exit 255) is unresolved.
next_steps: Confirm with the platform owner which log index/cluster tag holds production-eu-west-2 application logs, and whether app-264-prod-logs was expected to be a production index but is being written with staging labels.

Once Prometheus is reachable, compare checkout's error-rate and gRPC status series (traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name,status_code}, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count{rpc_service,rpc_method,rpc_grpc_status_code}) inside 2026-11-21T05:13:57Z–06:13:57Z against an earlier comparable window before claiming any latency or error trend.
Once Jaeger is reachable, pull error spans for checkout in the production scope and follow only parent references that the spans actually carry to identify the failing downstream call.

Verify in the production cluster whether any fault-injection or credential setting (for example a payment-provider API key or a flagd-style fault flag) is enabled; secrets could not be read here, so any such value remains unverified.
